section_summary: This section documents the fallout and political reaction to General Douglas MacArthur's July 22, 1948 letter to Prime Minister Ashida Hitoshi, which directed a comprehensive revision of Japan's National Public Service Law to prohibit strikes and collective bargaining by government employees. It traces the Japanese government's immediate enforcement of this policy through Cabinet Order No. 201 and public statements, accompanied by extensive Japanese press commentary largely endorsing the ban while urging better civil service working conditions. It also details high-level dissent and labor opposition, notably the resignation of GHQ Labor Division Chief James S. Killen over the denial of collective bargaining rights, and defiant pushback from leftist union leaders.

subfiles.about: Transmits copies of General Douglas MacArthur's letter to Prime Minister Ashida Hitoshi regarding revision of the National Public Service Law.
subfiles.from: Acting Political Adviser, Tokyo (W. J. Sebald)
subfiles.summary: Cover despatch forwarding MacArthur's July 22 letter directing revision of the National Public Service Law to ban civil service strikes.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 465: Letter from General MacArthur to Prime Minister Regarding National Public Service Law

subfiles.about: Public release quoting General MacArthur's letter calling for immediate revision of the National Public Service Law to eliminate strikes and collective bargaining in the civil service.
subfiles.from: Public Information Office, General Headquarters, Far East Command
subfiles.summary: General Douglas MacArthur advises Prime Minister Ashida Hitoshi that government workers owe undivided allegiance to the public trust and cannot be permitted to strike or obstruct government operations. Citing Franklin D. Roosevelt, he distinguishes public employment from private enterprise and states that collective bargaining cannot be transplanted into public administration. He recommends immediate revision of the National Public Service Law, suggests public corporations for railways and state monopolies, and urges reorganization of the Ministry of Communications.
subfiles.title: GHQ FEC Press Release: Letter from General Douglas MacArthur to Prime Minister Ashida Hitoshi Regarding the National Public Service Law
subfiles.to: Press Corps / Prime Minister Ashida Hitoshi

subfiles.about: Analyzes Japanese press reactions and editorial commentary following General MacArthur's letter recommending revision of the National Public Service Law.
subfiles.from: Acting Political Adviser, Tokyo (W. J. Sebald)
subfiles.summary: Reports that major Japanese dailies overwhelmingly supported MacArthur's strike ban, while urging improved wages for public workers and warning against union politicization.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 491: Japanese Reaction to Supreme Commander's Letter Concerning Revision of Public Service Law

subfiles.about: Presents communist criticisms of the proposed National Public Service Law revision and quotes NCIU Chairman Kan condemning restrictions on labor's right to strike.
subfiles.summary: Akahata denounces the government's move to revise the civil service law, while NCIU Chairman Kan asserts the government is suppressing labor's constitutional right to strike.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 1 to Despatch No. 491: Protect Human Rights (Akahata Editorial and Report)

subfiles.about: Editorial explaining that public employees exercise sovereign state power and therefore cannot strike or subordinate public interest to private union demands.
subfiles.summary: Endorses MacArthur's letter, arguing that public servants owe allegiance to the sovereign people and cannot engage in strikes against the government.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 2 to Despatch No. 491: The Nature of Public Service (Nippon Times Editorial)

subfiles.about: Discusses proposed revisions to the National Public Service Law, supporting dispute bans for civil servants while urging inflation relief for government workers.
subfiles.summary: Backs the ban on public worker strikes and slowdowns, but emphasizes that the government and Diet must address inflation hardships affecting civil service living standards.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 3 to Despatch No. 491: Amendments to National Public Service Act (Asahi Shimbun Editorial)

subfiles.about: Reflects on the SCAP letter, reproaching the government and unions for incompetence while calling for adequate employee welfare protections.
subfiles.summary: Criticizes the government, Diet, and unions for failing to resolve disputes independently, while urging fair compensation and safeguards for public employees.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 4 to Despatch No. 491: Reflections Apropos of SCAP Letter (Mainichi Shimbun Editorial)

subfiles.about: Editorial urging self-introspection by government and union leaders following General MacArthur's letter restricting public employee dispute tactics.
subfiles.summary: Editorial calling for introspection by authorities and unions over mishandled labor disputes, emphasizing the need to safeguard public employee living standards.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 5 to Despatch No. 491: Need For Self-Introspection (The Mainichi Editorial)

subfiles.about: Calls for normalizing the Japanese labor movement along democratic lines in harmony with public interest following MacArthur's letter.
subfiles.summary: Welcomes clarification of the boundary between public and private employment, urging unions to avoid partisan manipulation and pursue healthy, democratic development.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 6 to Despatch No. 491: We Expect Normalization of Labor Movement (Yomiuri Shimbun Editorial)

subfiles.about: Press summary quoting Yomiuri's argument that denying public workers strike rights obligates the Diet and public to ensure fair compensation.
subfiles.summary: Argues that stripping civil servants of strike rights requires the public and Diet, rather than bureaucrats alone, to guarantee fair wages.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 7 to Despatch No. 491: Public Servant's Treatment & Public Opinion (Nippon Times Press Comments Quoting Yomiuri)

subfiles.about: Full translation of Yomiuri editorial analyzing constitutional aspects of civil service strike restrictions and demanding popular representation on personnel welfare councils.
subfiles.summary: Contends that while stripping public servants of strike rights is constitutional under Article 15, the Diet and public must guarantee adequate salaries and reject undemocratic bureaucratic control.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 8 to Despatch No. 491: Treatment of Officials and Opinion of People (Yomiuri Shimbun Editorial)

subfiles.about: Laments that Japanese society lacked the initiative and public opinion to stop political strikes without repeated Occupation intervention.
subfiles.summary: Criticizes the public's lack of initiative and civic responsibility in allowing politically motivated public sector strikes to require repeated SCAP interventions.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 9 to Despatch No. 491: Reflections Regarding Civil Servants' Strikes (Jiji Shimpo Editorial)

subfiles.about: Brief editorial warning private labor unions that wildcat strikes and political plots by government workers forced the legislative restrictions.
subfiles.summary: Warns labor unions that irresponsible wildcat strikes and political agitation by government workers necessitated the legal restrictions on civil service disputes.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 10 to Despatch No. 491: Obligations of Public Officials (Nihon Keizai Shimbun Editorial)

subfiles.about: Urges union leaders to heed MacArthur's letter and calls on the Diet to reform labor legislation to secure industrial peace and foreign investment.
subfiles.summary: Urges union executives to abandon radical leftist agitation and calls on the Diet to revise labor laws to ensure industrial peace and attract foreign capital.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 11 to Despatch No. 491: Study SCAP's Letter Well (Tokyo Shimbun Editorial)

subfiles.about: Reports military intelligence revealing government worker unions planned to appeal MacArthur's strike ban to the Allied Council for Japan.
subfiles.from: Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Reports G-2 intelligence indicating government worker unions (Zen-Kankō) planned to request Allied Council intervention, possibly prompting Soviet member action against the strike ban.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-163: National Liaison Council of Government and Public Office Workers' Unions Plans to Appeal to Allied Council

subfiles.about: Transmits texts of Cabinet Order No. 201 and accompanying government statement temporarily prohibiting strikes and collective bargaining by public employees.
subfiles.from: Acting Political Adviser, Tokyo (W. J. Sebald)
subfiles.summary: Transmits English and Japanese texts of Cabinet Order No. 201 temporarily suspending collective bargaining and mediation while banning strikes by public employees.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 503: Cabinet Order Issued as Result of Supreme Commander's Letter Concerning Revision of National Public Service Law

subfiles.about: Official English translation of Cabinet Order No. 201 enacting temporary prohibitions on collective bargaining and strikes by national and local public employees.
subfiles.summary: Promulgates temporary prohibitions on collective bargaining and strikes by national and local public employees, establishing penalties up to one year imprisonment or 5,000 yen fine.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 1 to Despatch No. 503: Cabinet Order Concerning the Temporary Measures to be Taken in Consequence of the Letter of the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers to the Prime Minister Dated July 22, 1948

subfiles.about: Official Japanese text of Cabinet Order No. 201 establishing temporary measures restricting public servants' labor disputes.
subfiles.summary: Official Japanese text of Cabinet Order No. 201 prohibiting strikes and collective bargaining by national and local public employees pending statutory Diet amendments.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 2 to Despatch No. 503: Japanese Text of Cabinet Order No. 201

subfiles.about: Official statement explaining the promulgation of Cabinet Order No. 201 pursuant to SCAP's letter, restricting public worker dispute tactics.
subfiles.summary: Statement clarifying that the ordinance temporarily bans public employee strikes and collective bargaining per SCAP directive, while maintaining peaceful negotiation rights and wage review plans.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 3 to Despatch No. 503: Government Statement Accompanying Cabinet Order No. 201

subfiles.about: Reports reactions of Japanese government officials, political figures, and labor leaders to MacArthur's letter, the cabinet order, and the resignation of GHQ Labor Division Chief Killen.
subfiles.from: Acting Political Adviser, Tokyo (W. J. Sebald)
subfiles.summary: Despatch analyzing varied Japanese and Occupation reactions to General MacArthur's letter and the resulting Cabinet Order banning public employee strikes. Deputy Chief Cabinet Secretary Fukushima and other leaders discuss legal enforcement, civil service exemptions, and political prospects for the Ashida Cabinet. It highlights sharp labor hostility, including communist-backed resistance from union leaders Dobashi and Kan, as well as the controversy surrounding Labor Division Chief James S. Killen's protest resignation over the denial of collective bargaining rights. Political Adviser Sebald concludes that MacArthur's intervention averted a crippling August labor offensive and brought needed stability.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 514: Reaction of Japanese Leaders to National Public Service Law

subfiles.about: Killen's public statement clarifying that his resignation protested the denial of collective negotiation and arbitration rights to 2.5 million government workers.
subfiles.from: James S. Killen (former Chief, Labor Division, ESS, GHQ)
subfiles.summary: Killen clarifies his resignation was not against anti-strike bans but against stripping 2.5 million government workers of collective bargaining, mediation, and arbitration rights.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 1 to Despatch No. 514: Personal Statement Made by Mr. James S. Killen to the American Press

subfiles.about: Records Killen's farewell discussion with Sebald detailing his policy clashes with Hoover and Whitney and warning of communist gains and super-bureaucracy.
subfiles.summary: Records Killen's farewell visit, where he criticized Blaine Hoover and General Whitney's policies, warned of impending communist infiltration, and predicted a repressive super-bureaucracy.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 2 to Despatch No. 514: Memorandum of Conversation Between W. J. Sebald and James S. Killen

subfiles.about: Blaine Hoover's rebuttal dismissing Killen's position as pure nonsense and defending MacArthur's intervention to avert a crippling public sector strike.
subfiles.from: Public Information Office, General Headquarters, Far East Command
subfiles.summary: Blaine Hoover dismisses Killen's stance as nonsense, asserting MacArthur acted decisively to prevent a catastrophic strike, eradicate feudal bureaucracy, and stop communist infiltration.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 3 to Despatch No. 514: GHQ FEC Press Release on Blaine Hoover's Comments Regarding James S. Killen's Statement
